use_when: Use it for one digit of a code, such as a sign-in or verification code.
Use Typed once that cell holds a digit. Use Default while it is empty.
Use Hovered as pointer feedback only. It does not mean the cell holds a digit.
Use Error when the code is wrong. The border carries the status.

dont_use_when.when: Do not use one cell for a whole code. A code is a row of cells.
Do not use it for a name, email, or password.
Do not detach the instance to recolor a status border.
Do not override the cell size. It is fixed at 52 by 56 so a row of cells aligns.
Do not put more than one digit in Value.

variant_intent.State=Default: Use Typed once that cell holds a digit. Use Default while it is empty.
variant_intent.State=Typed: Use Typed once that cell holds a digit. Use Default while it is empty.
variant_intent.State=Hovered: Use Hovered as pointer feedback only. It does not mean the cell holds a digit.
variant_intent.State=Error: Use Error when the code is wrong. The border carries the status.
variant_intent.State=Disabled: Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.

placement: In a row, one cell per digit, between the explanation ('Check your inbox') and the Primary 'Verify email' button, in the Figma 'Component Appearance' example.

a11y.fact: A real text input: the digit is its value, with inputMode numeric, autoComplete one-time-code and maxLength 1.
The cell has an accessible name from the label prop (aria-label); each cell needs its own, for example "Digit 1 of 6".
State=Disabled sets the real DOM disabled attribute.
Implement Disabled in code, not just visually. Color alone is not enough.
Keyboard focus is not in this set yet. Do not treat hover as a substitute.
